name: CS-Ray
author: hamed7ir
description: CS-Ray is a proxy client for Windows that I wrote fully in C#. There is no xray.exe or sing-box inside it. The protocols, the TLS and the TUN network stack are all managed .NET code, so it runs on old ARM32 Windows where v2rayN and the other clients can't. It supports VLESS over TCP, WebSocket and XHTTP with TLS or REALITY and XTLS Vision, VMess (AEAD), Shadowsocks (AEAD), and SOCKS5 or HTTP(S) servers. You get a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:10810 with two modes on top: system proxy, or a full tunnel (Wintun) that takes all the traffic of the PC. Links it can't run yet (Trojan, Hysteria, TUIC, gRPC) still get imported, greyed out with the reason. One build runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1, Windows 10 ARM32, and x86 and x64 Windows 7 and newer. On Windows 7 only system proxy mode works, because the Wintun driver needs Windows 8. RT 8.0 needs the .NET 4.8 update.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.7 or newer
Windows RT 8.0 only: the .NET Framework 4.8 update. It's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
You need .NET Framework 4.7 or newer. Windows 10 and 11 already have it. If you're not sure, the installer has a Check requirements button.
On Windows RT 8.0 install the .NET Framework 4.8 update first. The app won't start without it, and it's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
Run CS-Ray-Setup-2.0.0.exe. It installs only for your user (to %LocalAppData%\Programs\CS-Ray) and doesn't need admin.
Add a server from a link or add a subscription, pick a server and start it. The local SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy is on 127.0.0.1:10810.

System proxy mode never needs admin. Full tunnel asks for admin (UAC) because it makes a Wintun network adapter. When you're done, close CS-Ray from the tray icon (Exit) so it can remove the adapter and the routes.
On Windows 7 use system proxy mode. Full tunnel needs Windows 8 or newer, because the Wintun driver does.

name: DroidFinestra (x64)
author: hamed7ir
description: DroidFinestra lets you use your Android phone from Windows. It's a GUI for scrcpy, so you can see and control the phone over USB or Wi-Fi. You keep a profile for each phone, it builds the scrcpy command for you, pairs phones over Wi-Fi and shows scrcpy's output. This package has the official scrcpy release with Google's adb, and it runs on 64-bit Windows 10 and 11. It needs .NET Framework 4.0 and, for adb, the Universal C Runtime. Windows 10 and 11 already have both. DroidFinestra starts scrcpy but doesn't change it. scrcpy is made by Genymobile.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or newer. Windows 10 and 11 already have it.
The Universal C Runtime, for the adb inside. Windows 10 and 11 already have it.
USB debugging turned on, on the Android phone.
instructionSteps: Run the installer. It installs for your user only into %LocalAppData%\Programs\DroidFinestra and doesn't need admin. It checks the requirements first and tells you if something is missing.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
On the phone, turn on USB debugging (in Developer options), connect it by USB and accept the USB debugging prompt on the phone.
In DroidFinestra choose New profile, start from a preset and press Launch. You see the scrcpy command line first, then scrcpy's live output.

For Wi-Fi: on the phone open Wireless debugging and choose Pair device with pairing code. In DroidFinestra open the menu, choose Pair a phone over Wi-Fi, and type the pairing address and code, then the connect address. You type the addresses, they are not found automatically.

name: Finestra
author: hamed7ir
description: Finestra is a remote connection manager: RDP, SSH, SFTP, FTP and FTPS in one app, with tabs. I made it mainly for Windows RT, because there is no good modern remote desktop client for it. For RDP it uses FreeRDP 3.32.2 (the SDL3 client) with my changes, built for ARM32 and x64. On a touch screen there is a Touch / Mouse switch, so swipe and pinch go to the remote PC. One build runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1, Windows 10 ARM32, and x86 and x64 Windows 10 and 11. You need .NET Framework 4.7 or newer, and on RT 8.0 that means the .NET 4.8 update, which is hard to find right now. On 32-bit x86 Windows you have to add the RDP engine yourself, SSH and FTP work without it. The files are not signed, and Windows RT has to be jailbroken.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.7 or newer
Windows RT 8.0 only: the .NET Framework 4.8 update. It's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
instructionSteps: Install .NET Framework 4.7 or newer if you don't have it. Windows 10 1703 and later already have it.
On Windows RT 8.0 install the .NET Framework 4.8 update first. The app won't start without it, and it's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
Run Finestra-Setup-2.0.0.exe. It installs for your user only into %LocalAppData%\Programs\Finestra, with no admin needed. You get a Start menu shortcut and an uninstall entry.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from 1.0.3: install into the same folder and your connections and settings are kept. If you set your own engine path in Settings > RDP engine, clear it, or you keep the old engine.
On a touch screen RDP starts in Touch mode. You can change it with the switch on the tab bar or in Settings > Session.
On 32-bit x86 Windows you have to add the RDP engine yourself. Read README.txt in engine\x86. SSH and FTP work without it.

name: Lite XL
author: Lite XL Team
description: Lite XL is a text editor written mostly in Lua, made from rxi's lite. Upstream doesn't make a 32-bit ARM Windows build, so this is my unofficial build of Lite XL 2.1.8. I tested it on Windows RT 8.0, Windows RT 8.1 and Windows 10 ARM32. The C runtime is built in, so the editor needs nothing else installed. The installer in this package needs .NET Framework 4.0, which Windows RT already has. It installs for your user only and doesn't ask for admin.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0, only for the installer. Windows RT already has it. The editor itself needs nothing.
instructionSteps: Extract lite-xl-2.1.8-arm32-windows-setup.zip anywhere. You get a folder named lite-xl-2.1.8-arm32-windows-setup.
Open that folder and run LiteXLSetup.exe. The installer isn't signed, so Windows warns about an unknown publisher.
Pick an install folder, or keep the default %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Lite XL.
Tick the Start menu shortcut, Desktop shortcut and right-click entry you want, then press Install.
It installs for your user only and doesn't need admin.
To remove it later, use Settings > Apps, or run LiteXLUninstall.exe in the install folder.

name: TelegArm
author: hamed7ir
description: TelegArm is a Telegram client for Windows RT and Windows 10 ARM32. The official Telegram apps don't run on these devices anymore, so I made this one. It runs on normal Windows PCs too. It's written in C# and talks to Telegram with WTelegramClient. Voice calls, video calls and group voice chats use Telegram's own call library (tgcalls), and videos and music play with FFmpeg. One build runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1, Windows 10 ARM32, and Windows 8.1, 10 and 11 (x86, x64 and ARM64). Calls need Windows 8.1 or newer. Windows 7 is not tested yet, and calls don't work there. You need .NET Framework 4.7 or newer. Windows RT 8.1 comes with 4.5, so install 4.7 first, and RT 8.0 needs the .NET 4.8 update, which is hard to find.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.7 or newer
Windows RT 8.0 only: the .NET Framework 4.8 update. It's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
Windows 8.1 or newer for voice and video calls
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
Install .NET Framework 4.7 or newer first. On Windows RT 8.1 get it here: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2088632. Windows 10 ARM32 already has it.
On Windows RT 8.0 install the .NET Framework 4.8 update first. The app won't start without it, and it's hard to find for RT 8.0 right now.
Run TelegArm-2.0.0-Setup.exe. It checks .NET for you and gives you the link if it's missing.
Voice and video calls need Windows 8.1 or newer.
On Windows 7 also install the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 or newer redistributable (x86). TelegArm works without it, but animated stickers won't move.
Upgrading from 1.9: your accounts and settings carry over.

name: Varan
author: Moonchild Productions
description: Varan is Pale Moon built for 32-bit ARM Windows, for tablets like the Surface RT and Surface 2. Pale Moon doesn't make ARM32 builds, so I made this fork. It runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1 and Windows 10 ARM32. Version 1.1 is based on Pale Moon 35.0.0 (UXP RB_20260914), with ARM NEON for libvpx and ARM code for ffvpx, so 720p and 1080p video plays. Your device has to be in test-signing mode, because Windows RT won't load unsigned ARM programs otherwise. You also need the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 or newer redistributable for ARM32. Varan is not made or supported by Moonchild Productions, so please report bugs to me, not to the Pale Moon project.
dependencies: Windows test-signing mode on the device, so the unsigned ARM programs can run.
Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 or newer redistributable for ARM32. varan.exe needs VCRUNTIME140.dll and the Universal CRT, and they are not in the package.
The vorapis v3 extension (https://vorapis.pages.dev/#/home/download), only for YouTube. It's third party and not in the package.
instructionSteps: Put the device in test-signing mode.
Install the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015 or newer redistributable for ARM32 if you don't have it. varan.exe needs VCRUNTIME140.dll and the Universal CRT.
Extract Varan-35.0.0-arm32-Setup.zip. You get a folder named Varan-Setup with Setup.exe and payload.zip in it.
Keep Setup.exe and payload.zip together and run Setup.exe. It installs for your user only, and uninstalling keeps your profile.
Start Varan from its shortcut.
For YouTube, install the vorapis v3 extension from https://vorapis.pages.dev/#/home/download. It's third party and not in the package.
It's a good idea to remove the old profile from %APPDATA% (C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming) and start fresh.

name: Venetium (x86)
author: hamed7ir
description: Venetium is Chromium 150 (150.0.7871.226) tuned for 2 GB devices, with a built-in ad and tracker blocker (EasyList and EasyPrivacy) that is on by default. This is the 32-bit x86 build. It needs Windows 10 or newer, and it runs on 64-bit Windows too. It's built on Supermium and ungoogled Chromium. The ARM32 build for the Surface RT and Surface 2 is a separate entry.
instructionSteps: Run Venetium-Setup-150.0.7871.226-x86.exe. It installs for your user only, with shortcuts and an uninstaller, and doesn't need admin.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from v1.0: just install v1.2 over it.
The ad and tracker blocker is on by default. To allow a site, use the "ads blocked" icon in the address bar, or turn the blocker off in chrome://settings/content/ads.

name: Venetium
author: hamed7ir
description: Venetium is Chromium 150 (150.0.7871.226) for old ARM Windows tablets: the Surface RT (Tegra 3) and Surface 2 (Tegra 4) on Windows 10 build 15035. I wanted a real modern browser on these tablets, and nothing new runs on them anymore. It's built on Supermium and ungoogled Chromium, and the ARM32 port is my own work. Graphics go through Direct3D 9 and ANGLE, because these GPUs have no Direct3D 11. H.264 video is decoded on the GPU, so 720p plays smooth, and the sandbox is on. It has a built-in ad and tracker blocker (EasyList and EasyPrivacy) that is on by default, and it's tuned for 2 GB tablets. Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1 are not supported yet.
instructionSteps: Run Venetium-Setup-150.0.7871.226-arm32.exe. It installs for your user only, with shortcuts and an uninstaller, and doesn't need admin.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
Upgrading from v1.0: just install v1.2 over it.
The ad and tracker blocker is on by default. To allow a site, use the "ads blocked" icon in the address bar, or turn the blocker off in chrome://settings/content/ads.

name: Xtreme Download Manager
author: Subhra Das Gupta
description: Xtreme Download Manager 8.0.29, set up to run on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1 and Windows 10 ARM32. It downloads over HTTP and HTTPS in many parts at once, and it can resume. Video download doesn't work, because yt-dlp and ffmpeg are x86 programs and can't run on ARM32. This is my unofficial fork of subhra74/xdm. I didn't change any source code, only the icon. It needs .NET Framework 4.5 or newer and WPF. Windows RT has no WPF, so you have to install an ARM32 WPF build once with wpf-prerequisite\wpf-setup.cmd (it's in the package) before XDM will start.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.5 or newer. On Windows RT 8.1 install the RT package from https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2088632 (it shows up as KB4486105).
KB2919355, the Windows RT 8.1 Update. The .NET package won't install without it.
WPF for ARM32. It's not in the package and I can't share it. Get the ARM32 WPF port from XDA and install it once with wpf-prerequisite\wpf-setup.cmd.
Windows test-signing mode on the device, because the files are not signed.
instructionSteps: Install KB2919355 (the Windows RT 8.1 Update) if you don't have it.
Install the .NET Framework package for Windows RT from https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2088632, and reboot when it asks.
Put the device in test-signing mode, so unsigned desktop apps can run.
Extract XDM-8.0.29-rt1-Setup-AnyCPU.zip. Keep Setup.exe and payload.zip together.
Download the ARM32 WPF port from https://xdaforums.com/t/wpf-for-windows-rt-devices.3763345/ and extract it next to wpf-prerequisite\wpf-setup.cmd.
Run wpf-prerequisite\wpf-setup.cmd /verify to see what's missing. It doesn't change anything and doesn't need admin.
Run wpf-prerequisite\wpf-setup.cmd as Administrator to install WPF.
Run Setup.exe --check to see if everything is in place. It doesn't change anything.
Run Setup.exe to install XDM for your user, then start XDM from the Start menu.
